messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A removable sensor bracket on a test rig. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i press the bracket against the fastener with my palm, then test the loose part with a pencil. the reading shows no trouble, so i mark the bracket’s edge with pencil and place it under the fastener. i keep the pencil in case the fastener remains."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i press the fastener against the bracket and check the sensor cable. the loose bracket moves, but the sensor reads fine. i move it back and check the cable. sorry—sorry, i’m photographing the sensor instead of touching it."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "you put the bracket on the step. you listen. the loose part moves. you put the fastener back. the readings stay normal. you watch the rig. the bracket stays loose."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i press the fastener against the bracket. the loose bolt catches. i move the bracket closer, then tap the fastener twice. “not loose,” i say. “not normal.” i leave the bolt loose enough to measure later."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "i rub my palm and watch the fastener move. i set it back on the bench, then test the bracket once more. if the loose fastener moves, i stop and try the fastener. if the sensor feels loose, i mark the bracket and keep it."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i tighten the bracket with my thumb and mark the loose side with chalk. i test the bracket again with the loose one and mark the mark with chalk. i leave it there for a moment, then tighten the bracket once more."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "the fastener ticks. the bracket shifts. i press the bracket with the wrench. the tick stays. i tap the bracket with the wrench. the tick stops. the bracket stays. i press the bracket with the wrench until the light catches. the bracket stays. i tap the bracket with the wrench and the light catches. the bracket stays. i remove the fastener. the tick comes back. the bracket stays."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "Remove the fastener. The bracket is loose. I press it down. The reading is wrong. I check the ruler. One ruler is wrong. I replace it. The bracket is not loose. I keep the fastener."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i press the fastener into the ground with my thumbnail. the loose part catches and shifts, so i keep the bracket beside the rig. i leave the sensor intact because the loose part might reveal a hidden spring. i leave the sensor loose enough to measure the axle and gear shifts."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i press the fastener down and check the bracket's position. it feels almost cracked, so i move it a little and wait a second. the readings stay normal, so i keep watching the bracket. i put the fastener back in and wait a second."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i put the fastener under the loose bracket and leave the sensor loose. the readings come back. i stop with the loose one. the fastener can stay in one place. i leave the sensor where it is."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i press the bracket down once, then tap the page edge twice. “fine,” i say, and hold the fastener against the rig. the loose fastener catches the page edge, so i tap the bracket twice with my fingertip instead of the nail. the loose fastener slides free and lands beside the sensor."}]
